title: Why Awareness Matters: Creating Opportunities for Preventative Care
summary: Breast Cancer Awareness Month serves as an important reminder that early detection can save lives.
body_markdown:
**By Sarah Wade,** **Account Manager, International F/T Sales**


Breast Cancer Awareness Month serves as an important reminder that early detection can save lives. This year, I had the opportunity to help organize an event that brought that message directly to life for our employees and their families.


On October 6, our Women’s Employee Resource Group in Apex, North Carolina, partnered with the Rex Mobile Mammography Unit to provide on-site mammogram screenings for employees and their spouses. Our goal was simple: Make preventative healthcare more accessible while encouraging conversations about breast health, early detection, and wellness.


While access to screenings was a key part of the event, what made the day especially meaningful was the visible support demonstrated throughout our community. Employees wore pink to raise awareness and show solidarity with those affected by breast cancer. Across the campus, colleagues came together in a shared commitment to health, wellness, and supporting one another.


One of the most memorable moments came when we recognized **Annie Judd, Quality Assurance Electrical Technician,** and breast cancer survivor. Honoring her with a special photo frame highlighted the human side of why awareness efforts matter. Their strength and resilience served as a powerful reminder that cancer impacts real people, families, and communities.


Events like this reinforce something I deeply believe: Supporting employee wellbeing extends beyond programs and policies. It means creating opportunities that make it easier for people to prioritize their health and take proactive steps toward preventative care.


I am grateful to everyone who participated, whether by scheduling a screening, wearing pink, helping organize activities, or simply showing support. Every conversation, every act of encouragement, and every step toward preventative care contributes to a stronger, healthier community.


Breast cancer awareness is about more than a single day or month. It is about continuing to educate, support, and empower people to take action for themselves and their loved ones. If this event encouraged even one person to schedule a screening they might otherwise have postponed, it made a meaningful difference.


Together, we can continue building a culture that prioritizes health, supports one another through challenges, and reminds people that they are never alone on their journey.
